_source: bina-gtm/notes/ESA_State_Database.xlsx — the bina team's ESA database. This file lists ONLY the states where bina can accept students today; a state is added here the day its approval lands, never before. Sync from the database; never invent numbers or dates. If a field is unknown, use an honest fallback and flag the gap to the team.

_dates._note: Application windows researched 2026-09-22 against each state's own site. Re-verify every August, before the next cycle opens. Where a state has not published its dates, say so on the page rather than guessing.
_dates.Arizona: Rolling, no annual deadline. Quarterly cutoffs (Jun 1 / Sep 1 / Dec 1 / Mar 1) carried from the team database — azed.gov blocks automated fetches, so confirm by hand with ADE.
_dates.New Hampshire: nh.scholarshipfund.org — rolling; full award needs the application complete and verified by Jul 15, documents in by Jul 1; prorated awards through February. 2027–28 open date not published; 2026–27 opened Mar 16, 2026.
_dates.Utah: utaheducationfitsall.org — Mar 1 returning / Apr 1 new / May 1 close is the recurring schedule set in law, so the 2027 dates follow from statute rather than an announcement.
_dates.Idaho: Idaho State Tax Commission — Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027 published for the 2026 credit paid in 2027. Priority from 2027: prior-year recipients, then ≤300% FPL.
_dates.Wyoming: edu.wyoming.gov and the WDE bulletin — 2026–27 opened 9 a.m. Jul 6, 2026, processed by end of July, funds by Sep 1. 2027–28 dates NOT published as of 2026-09-22.

_retired: allStates is every US state, kept for ONE reason: astro.config.mjs turns every state that is not in `programs` into a redirect to /esa. Those 45 pages existed (PR #36 built one per state); killing them outright would 404 links that are already out there, so they redirect instead. Do not use allStates to build pages — `programs` is the list of states we can serve.

programs.who: Every Arizona K–12 family — no income requirement.
programs.howMuch: $7,000–$8,000 per child, per year (more for children with special needs).
programs.applyWindow: Open all year — Arizona has no annual deadline. Your funding quarter is set by the date you sign with bina, with cutoffs on Jun 1, Sep 1, Dec 1 and Mar 1, so signing earlier means funds sooner.
programs.windowNote: Arizona is the one state you can start in any month of the year.
programs.approval: Approval takes up to 30 days. You pre-register, then set up ClassWallet and link your bank. Because your funding quarter is set by your contract-signing date, signing with bina early puts you in an earlier funding quarter.
programs.boost: Arizona's handbook explicitly approves “tuition or fees for a nonpublic online learning program” — exactly the category bina is in.

programs.who: Idaho families with a child in nonpublic school (ages 5–19).
programs.howMuch: Up to $5,000 per child, per year ($7,500 for children with special needs).
programs.applyWindow: Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027, through your Idaho Taxpayer Access Point (TAP) account. It is first come, first served, and from 2027 priority goes to families who received the credit the year before, then to households at or below 300% of the federal poverty level.
programs.windowNote: The 2026 windows have closed. The next one runs Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027 — and because it is first come, first served, being ready matters more here than anywhere else.
programs.approval: This is a tax credit or an advance payment, not a school account: you apply, submit your bina tuition receipts, and Idaho pays you — either as a refundable credit or as an advance payment. We give you every receipt and document your claim needs.

programs.who: Every New Hampshire K–12 family — the income cap was removed in 2025. Enrollment is capped statewide at 12,500 students, so apply early.
programs.applyWindow: Rolling, all year. For a full 2027–28 award your application must be complete and verified by Jul 15, 2027 — send your documents by Jul 1 to leave time for verification. Miss that and you can still get a prorated award for the year already underway, right through the end of February.
programs.windowNote: Rolling applications make New Hampshire, like Arizona, a state you can join mid-year.
programs.approval: Expect a response within about 30 days; if they ask for more documents it can take up to two months. Funds then arrive in four installments (September, November, January, April).

programs.who: Every Utah K–12 family (awards are limited, so not everyone who applies is funded).
programs.applyWindow: Mar 1, 2027 for returning students and their siblings, Apr 1, 2027 for new students, and the portal closes May 1, 2027. These dates are set in Utah law and repeat every year.
programs.windowNote: The 2026–27 window closed on May 1, 2026. The next one opens Mar 1, 2027 — families who talk to us now are ready on day one.
programs.approval: Approval takes about a month, awards are announced in mid-June and you accept by the end of June. Awards are limited and not guaranteed, so we plan your bina start around your notification date rather than assuming the money.

programs.applyWindow: Wyoming has not published the 2027–28 dates yet. For 2026–27 the application opened at 9 a.m. on Jul 6, 2026, was processed by the end of July, and funds landed by Sep 1 — so plan for early July 2027. We will confirm the day the Wyoming Department of Education announces it.
programs.windowNote: The 2026–27 window closed at the end of July 2026 and the 2027–28 dates are not out yet. Expect early July 2027.
programs.approval: Wyoming verifies eligibility within about a month of the window closing, and your $7,000 lands in your Odyssey account by September 1. Returning families also get an extra $1,750 in rollover funds — we time your bina start to your funding date.
